taskA_pvcLabels.rootCause: apps/gateway/app/stores/manifests.py _db_statefulset built volumeClaimTemplates[0].metadata with only name 'data'. The StatefulSet controller creates data-store-db-0 from that template and adds the pod selector labels, so the claim got only app.kubernetes.io/component and app.kubernetes.io/name.
taskA_pvcLabels.severity: low: traceability and label-selector gap, not an isolation or deletion bug
whyNotSecurityCritical: Store deletion deletes namespace st-<id>; the claim goes with it.
Volume cleanup selects PersistentVolumes by spec.claimRef.namespace == st-<id>, not by PVC labels.
The provisioner never reads, updates, or deletes data-store-db-0; the StatefulSet controller owns it.
Admission matches only the provisioner ServiceAccount; the claim is created by the controller.
taskA_pvcLabels.liveClaim: data-store-db-0 Bound pvc-cfec2069-30de-43ee-b62f-7f02c16a7aa3, labels unchanged, not patched
sourceFix: manifests.py: claim template metadata.labels = labels(spec, 'store-db') (store-id, owner-id, store, name, component, managed-by, part-of)
cluster.py apply: when an existing StatefulSet is updated, keep the live spec.volumeClaimTemplates, because that field cannot change after create
taskA_pvcLabels.followUp: Only stores created after a new gateway image is deployed get labeled claims. acceptance-store-a keeps the unlabeled claim. Options: leave it (safe), or an owner-approved one-time 'kubectl --context kind-urumi-k8s-test label pvc data-store-db-0 -n st-c4421147ea825bbc urumi.dev/store-id=c4421147ea825bbc urumi.dev/owner-id=169d3b25942f065b urumi.dev/store=true'. That label write does not touch data.

taskB_authorization.registration: provisioner _register saves dynamic upstream store_<id> at http://woo-mcp.st-<id>.svc.cluster.local:8000/mcp; gateway registry lists its tools as store_<id>__<tool>
taskB_authorization.advertisedVsUsable: 6 tools advertised and registered; none listed or callable for the current key
taskB_authorization.listFilter: discovery.collect_authorized: exact grant on the key, then routing.store_block_reason
taskB_authorization.callCheck: dispatch.execute_tool: key active, exact grant, then store_call_allowed
taskB_authorization.storeRule: caller user_id equals store owner_user_id, store state ready, upstream id store_<id>, saved upstream enabled at the canonical URL
taskB_authorization.grantPath: POST /admin/keys/{key_id}/permissions by an admin; for a store tool the key must have user_id equal to the store owner
taskB_authorization.verdict: expected deny-by-default. The key was issued by 'provision issue', which creates a key with no owner, so the admin API refuses store grants for it and dispatch would deny it even if a grant row existed.
taskB_authorization.missingPrerequisite: a key owned by acceptance-admin (169d3b25942f065b), issued via POST /admin/keys, plus a grant of store_c4421147ea825bbc__list_orders. Both are live writes and were not done.
